new_statements.translation: 10. Tonetics. The tonetic character of the syllable in Olombo is as important as its phonetic quality. The pronunciation melody of a given word remains invariable except when the word appears at the end of a sentence that is not a question, or when it is uttered in isolation. In those cases the tone of the last syllable is always low and the tones of the other syllables of the word may undergo modifications [...] 11. There are only two essential tones, one low and the other high. [...] 12. In the notes that follow we mark the high-toned syllable with an acute accent; the low-toned syllable bears no accent.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Lombo is described as a two-tone (H/L) language with lexically and grammatically contrastive tone (minimal pairs given in section 13) and an utterance-final lowering ('final cadence') in isolation/declarative-final forms; the source makes no statement at all about word stress or an intensity accent.
new_statements.exceptions: None regarding stress. For tone: surface mid tones are contextual variants of H or L; citation/phrase-final forms get a final low with possible adjustments of preceding tones.
new_statements.domain_note: Tone statement is about the word; the final-lowering statement concerns words in isolation (citation forms) and declarative phrase-final position. Data from the Bosala (eastern) section of the Olombo area.
new_statements.identity_note: Carrington 1947 states (fn. 1, p. 102) that his notes are based on the Bosala (eastern) section of the Olombo; he names three tribal divisions with dialect differences (Yambau W/NW, Yangeka centre, Bosala E), mutually intelligible. Glottolog lomb1260 lists no sub-dialects, so the description maps to lomb1260 itself. 'Turumbu' is the administrative exonym for the same people/language (Carrington section 4 explains Tolombo > Turumbu).

sources.note: Nothing. Sections 5-13 (pp. 103-104) cover 7 vowels, length, vowel harmony, consonants and 'Tonetique': two essential tones (H, L), mid tone is contextual, in isolation/declarative-final position the last syllable is always low and other tones may shift (Hulstaert's 'ton pausal', Guthrie's 'final cadence'); high tone written with acute accent. No mention of accent d'intensite/stress anywhere in the article (grep of accent/intensite/penulti over the whole article: only the tone-marking sentence).
